title: Image Optimization with next/image
summary: Next.js Image helps load images with useful sizing and optimization features.

subtopics.title: Image component
subtopics.explanation: Import and use the `Image` component from `next/image`. It supports image sizing and optimization features in Next.js. It is like a picture frame that knows how to prepare its contents. Follow the current project’s Next.js version and configuration because supported options can change. For example, a fixed card ratio reserves space before a remote thumbnail has downloaded. In practice, reserve a thumbnail’s dimensions before a list response finishes loading.

subtopics.title: Reserve space
subtopics.explanation: Width and height describe the image proportions and help reserve its space before loading. This reduces layout shift. It is like leaving a correctly sized frame on the wall before the picture arrives. Supply dimensions that match the source or use a layout pattern that preserves its ratio. For example, use `fill` only after the parent has a measurable position and size. In practice, give the parent a defined box when using a fill layout.

subtopics.title: Fill a container
subtopics.explanation: Use `fill` when the parent element provides a sized container. The image then fills that area, often with `object-fit` controlling the crop. It is like placing a photo behind a fixed window. Ensure the parent has a size and test the crop at multiple screen widths. For example, a portrait headshot may need `object-position` so the face stays visible. In practice, check a portrait crop on both phone and desktop widths.

subtopics.title: Alt text
subtopics.explanation: Alt text describes what an informative image contributes. Decorative images should use empty alt text so they can be skipped. It is like a caption that can be read aloud. Do not repeat nearby text unless it adds useful information about the image. For example, a decorative hero image can have empty alternative text when its message is already in nearby text. In practice, a decorative image can use empty alt text when nearby content carries the meaning.

subtopics.title: Remote files
subtopics.explanation: Remote image hosts may need to be allowed in Next.js configuration. The setting limits which sources the image optimizer can fetch. It is like a guest list for an image service. Allow only the hosts the app needs, and verify remote images after deployment. For example, add a remote host narrowly instead of allowing every arbitrary image URL. In practice, allow only expected remote image hosts in configuration.

foundations.overview: Next.js provides the `Image` component to help load and size images in an application. It can reserve layout space and optimize supported image sources. Think of it as a smart picture frame that prepares an image for the available space. Provide meaningful alternative text, configure remote hosts when needed, and verify the result in production.
foundations.whyItMatters: Image handling affects loading speed, layout stability, and accessibility. Correct sizing and source rules help images behave predictably in production.
foundations.browserPerspective: The browser receives an with a generated srcset and reserved dimensions, so it can lay out the page immediately and pick the smallest source that fits the slot — and it defers loading off-screen images until they're near the viewport via native lazy loading.
foundations.realWorldUsage: A landing page marks the hero <Image priority>, product grids use fill + sizes inside aspect-ratio cards, and CMS-hosted images are enabled by adding the CMS hostname to remotePatterns.
foundations.businessImpact: Faster image loading and zero layout shift improve Core Web Vitals, which influence search ranking and conversion; smaller image payloads also cut bandwidth costs and improve experience on slow connections.
foundations.engineeringImpact: Developers stop hand-rolling srcset, manual resizing, and lazy-load libraries — one component standardizes image handling and removes a whole class of performance bugs from code review.
foundations.performanceImpact: Optimization cuts image bytes (resizing + WebP/AVIF), lazy-loading defers off-screen work, reserved dimensions kill CLS, and priority preloads the LCP image — collectively the biggest lever on most pages' Web Vitals.
commonUseCases: Hero/banner images marked priority for better LCP
Responsive product grids using fill + sizes inside aspect-ratio containers
Replacing raw tags to eliminate layout shift and oversized downloads
Render product photos at several viewport sizes.
Prevent a feed from jumping as images load.
Keep decorative and meaningful image descriptions distinct.

commonMisconceptions.myth: width/height on next/image set the fixed display size.
commonMisconceptions.reality: They set the intrinsic aspect ratio used to reserve space; CSS still controls how big the image actually renders (e.g. width:100%).

commonMisconceptions.myth: Adding priority to many images makes the page faster.
commonMisconceptions.reality: priority disables lazy-loading and preloads — use it only for the single above-the-fold LCP image; overusing it hurts performance.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Next Image guarantees every image is optimized in every environment.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Optimization depends on configuration, source, and deployment support; inspect the delivered asset.

commonMisconceptions.myth: A remote URL should be allowed from any host.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Restrict remote sources to trusted hosts and validate content ownership.

visualExplorer.title: What next/image does on load
visualExplorer.caption: Step through how next/image reserves space, optimizes, and loads an image.

config.intro: Follow one image from markup to a fast, shift-free render.

steps.name: Declare dimensions
steps.detail: You give width/height (or fill); Next uses the aspect ratio to reserve a correctly-sized box so the layout never jumps.

steps.name: Generate variants
steps.detail: The Image Optimization service produces resized versions and modern formats (WebP/AVIF) and caches them.

steps.name: Pick the source
steps.detail: Using srcset and the sizes hint, the browser downloads the smallest variant that fits the slot at the current viewport/DPR.

steps.name: Lazy or priority
steps.detail: Off-screen images lazy-load when near the viewport; the hero marked priority is preloaded for a faster LCP.

steps.name: Render shift-free
steps.detail: Because space was reserved up front, the image fades in without pushing content around — CLS stays at zero.

hints: The single above-the-fold image is your LCP — that's the one place for priority.
Use fill when you don't know the dimensions, and always pair fill with a sizes hint.

keyTakeaways: Import and use the `Image` component from `next/image`.
Width and height describe the image proportions and help reserve its space before loading.
Use `fill` when the parent element provides a sized container.
Alt text describes what an informative image contributes.
